testCases.name: Templates Endpoint HTTP 200
testCases.description: GET /v2/activities/templates returns HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 500 authentication error
testCases.rationale: After fixing signin() to include NS/DB parameters, authentication should succeed and templates endpoint should return HTTP 200 with valid JSON array response instead of HTTP 500 authentication error.

testCases.name: Activity API Connection Logs
testCases.description: Activity API logs show successful SurrealDB connection with namespace verification

expectedOutput.authErrorText: There was a problem with authentication (should NOT appear)

testCases.rationale: With proper NS/DB scope in signin(), Activity API should successfully authenticate and verify namespace access. Logs should contain success messages and no error messages.

testCases.name: SurrealDB Server Logs
testCases.description: SurrealDB logs show no authentication rejection errors
testCases.rationale: SurrealDB v3.0.0 server should accept authentication requests with proper NS/DB scope. No authentication rejection errors should appear in server logs.

testCases.name: Direct SurrealDB Connection
testCases.description: Direct SQL connection with kubectl exec using NS/DB scope succeeds

input.command: kubectl exec -n activity-system surrealdb-0 -- surreal sql --conn http://localhost:8000 --user root --pass <password> --ns activity-system --db learning_loop --pretty "INFO FOR NS;"

testCases.rationale: Direct connection to SurrealDB with proper NS/DB scope parameters should succeed. This validates that the authentication method (NS/DB in signin) works correctly at the protocol level.

testCases.name: Credentials Rendering
testCases.description: Kubernetes secret contains rendered credentials, not Helmfile template placeholders

commands: kubectl get secret -n activity-system surrealdb-credentials -o jsonpath="{.data.username}" | base64 -d
kubectl get secret -n activity-system surrealdb-credentials -o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 -d

testCases.rationale: Helmfile templates must be rendered during deployment. If secret contains literal '{{ env }}' strings, authentication will fail because credentials are invalid. This validates proper deployment process.

testCases.name: Namespace Configuration Consistency
testCases.description: Namespace configuration is consistent between Activity API and SurrealDB
testCases.rationale: Activity API expects 'activity-system' namespace after enforcement changes. Configuration must be consistent or authentication will fail when attempting to access non-existent namespace.

validationStrategy.description: Multi-layer validation of SurrealDB v3.0.0 authentication fix

layers.validates: Activity API successfully authenticates and queries work
SurrealDB accepts authentication with NS/DB scope

successCriteria.description: All test cases must pass for specification to be considered validated. Critical tests (1, 2, 4) are essential and their failure indicates authentication is still broken.
